title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes a 'tame topology' through a poset (F,≤) of 'figures', subject to axioms C1, C2, C3 stated earlier, roughly modelled on closed unions of strata of a stratified space. On page 59 he lets M be the poset of 'strata', i.e. the irreducible figures. He equips M with a reflexive, symmetric 'compatibility' relation R that is hereditary downward. He then tries to recover F, or at least its figures of finite type, from the triple (M,≤,R).

This page.
(1) The figures of finite type correspond to the subsets A ⊂ M (the image's '∈' means ⊂) of the form A = ∪_i A_{x_i}, where A_x = M_{≤x} is the closure of x, the x_i form a finite set, and the x_i are pairwise compatible for R.
(2) Hence a structure (F,≤) satisfying C1–C3 gives a structure of type (M,≤,R). Here ≤ is an order and R is a reflexive symmetric relation, subject to two conditions:
  (a) every closed (down-closed), bounded-above part A of M is of finite type, i.e. a finite union of the M_{≤x_i} with x_i ∈ A. The margin points to 'Cond 2 de la proposition page 33'. It suffices that every M_{≤x} be finite.
  (b) Compatibility of ≤ and R: if (x,y) ∈ R and x' ≤ x, y' ≤ y, then (x',y') ∈ R.
(3) Conversely the 'figures' of M are the parts A ⊂ M that are closed, of finite type, and pairwise compatible (∀x,y ∈ A, (x,y) ∈ R).

Page 61 states the resulting equivalence. Systems (F,≤) satisfying C1–C3 in which every figure has finitely many subfigures are the same thing as triples (M,≤,R) with each M_{≤x} finite and R downward hereditary. The figures are then the finite down-closed R-cliques. Page 61 then starts on connected components.

Modern reading. Call R 'consistency' and its complement 'conflict' #. Condition (b) is exactly conflict inheritance: x#y and y ≤ y' imply x#y'. 'M_{≤x} finite' is the finite-causes axiom. So (M,≤,#) is precisely a prime event structure in the sense of Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel (1981), and the figures are its finite configurations.

The reconstruction theorem (F recovered from its irreducibles plus binary compatibility) is the finitary form of the Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel / Winskel representation theorem: prime event structures correspond to prime-algebraic, finitary, coherent domains (dI-domains), with irreducible figures playing the role of complete primes. The 'pairwise compatible implies jointly a figure' clause is the coherence axiom. It is the same mechanism as Girard's coherence spaces (1987) and Berry's stable domains (1978). When R is total it reduces to Birkhoff's representation of finite distributive lattices by their join-irreducibles.

Purpose. To encode a combinatorial 'analysis situs' (stratified figures) by purely finite poset data plus a compatibility relation, before defining connectedness and components.
errors: 'A ∈ M' should read 'A ⊂ M' (A is a subset of M).

The description of finite-type figures as unions of closures of pairwise compatible elements silently assumes that pairwise compatibility suffices for a join to exist as a figure (a coherence/'flag' condition). This must come from axioms C1–C3, which are not shown here, and is not justified on this page.

Condition (a) is phrased for 'closed, bounded-above' parts. The parenthetical sufficient condition (M_{≤x} finite) makes it trivial, and page 61 replaces it by that finiteness condition. The general version is left vague.
The notation alternates between A_{x_i} and M_{≤x_i} for the same object (the closure of x_i).

ideas.what: Recover a poset of 'figures' from its poset of irreducibles (strata) plus a binary, downward-hereditary compatibility relation; figures are finite down-closed pairwise-compatible sets
ideas.modern_name: Prime event structures and finite configurations; representation of prime-algebraic coherent (dI-)domains; coherence spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen, Plotkin, Winskel (1981); Winskel (1980s); Berry (1978, stable domains); Girard (1987, coherence spaces)

ideas.what: Finite-type figures as finite unions of principal down-sets (closures of strata) in the Alexandrov topology of the strata poset
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov topology on a poset; Birkhoff representation via join-irreducibles
ideas.where_published: Close in spirit to the 'tame topology' programme of Esquisse d'un programme (1984), which does not give these axioms

ideas.what: Downward heredity of compatibility (if (x,y) ∈ R and x'≤x, y'≤y then (x',y') ∈ R)
ideas.modern_name: Conflict inheritance axiom of event structures

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatics of 'figures' in his combinatorial analysis situs independently reproduces prime event structures with finite causes and conflict inheritance. His reconstruction of (F,≤) from (M,≤,R) is the finitary Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel representation theorem. This places a 'tame topology'/stratified-space programme and concurrency/domain theory (stable domains, coherence spaces) on the same formal footing. That link does not appear to be noted in the literature on either side.
missed.quote: R rel. symétr. réfl. ... b) (compatibilité ≤ et R) si (x,y)∈R, et x'≤x, y'≤y, alors (x',y')∈R. Les "figures" de M sont les parties de M ... a) A est fermé b) A est de type fini c) ∀x,y∈A, on a (x,y)∈R.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Event structures and configuration spaces are studied topologically (directed topology, cubical models of concurrency, 'configuration structures'). Grothendieck's notes go on to connectedness and presumably further topological notions on such structures. They might offer a geometric (stratified-space) interpretation of event structures, or conversely give his analysis situs a ready-made semantic and combinatorial theory.

missed.claim: The non-finite case (condition (a): closed bounded parts of finite type, without assuming every M_{≤x} finite) is raised but immediately dropped in favour of finiteness on page 61. A representation of non-finitary figure systems by (M,≤,R) is left open.
missed.quote: a) partie fermée majorée A de M, A est de type fini ... [pour cela, il suffit que les M_{≤x} soient finis]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This corresponds to representation of non-finitary or non-prime-algebraic domains by event-structure-like data, a known subtle area. It is a minor thread.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary, essentially a Birkhoff-type representation. But the precise axioms (reflexive symmetric compatibility with downward heredity, finite principal down-sets, figures as finite down-closed cliques) coincide exactly with prime event structures and their configurations. Grothendieck apparently arrived at these in 1986 from stratified topology, independently of theoretical computer science. This cross-field coincidence seems unrecorded, but it is a rediscovery rather than a new result.

The left-margin vertical note reads approximately 'Vérifier dans le cas d'une figure finie [que la] figure finie [est] de type fini', followed by '(Cond 2 de proposition page 33)'. The transcription places part of this inline.
The insertion near a) reads '(concernant ≤)', and condition b) is labelled '(concernant ≤ et R)'.
